text:
maria: Heads-up — after the routing policy flip this morning we saw a spike of 429s for embeddings-only keys. Anyone else?
jon: saw it. Graph shows per-key bucket exhaustion even though per-org has spare capacity. Looks like we apply per-key burst first then org-level? :thinking_face: 
ethan: That's intended: per-key isolated burst to prevent noisy neighbor keys eating org quota. But maybe we didn't exempt embeddings endpoints from streaming-like long-lived request assumptions.
laura: embeddings should be charged in units not tokens, so their bucket decay is different. Are we using same token-burst policy for embed as chat?
maria: quick log snippet:
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640000000
```
Requests were tiny but frequent (~10ms intervals).
jon: That header looks like per-key 1.2k/min bucket; client hammered small requests — continuous small hits deplete faster than expected because we don't do prefix-caching for embeddings. Suggest tweak: allow short 5s micro-burst smoothing for embed endpoints.
ethan: Micro-burst smoothing is fine but need to consider cost: embeddings are cheap per unit but high QPS. Also dashboard needs to show per-endpoint burst consumption or SRE will be blind.
laura: +1 on dashboard. Proposed columns: endpoint, per-key-burst, org-remaining, rolling-60s-peak, top-keys. Could we also feed this into alerts when top key > 50% org-burst?
maria: Also observed streaming clients hitting chat with long-lived SSE connections causing token backlog vs embedding's short RPCs. Maybe separate enforcement model: streaming -> connection slots + token throughput; embed/rerank -> request-rate units.
jon: Agreed. For streaming we should have 'concurrency slots' and 'per-connection token rate', with a soft-fallback to lower-capacity model if exceeded.
ethan: Internals: current limiter stack = tokenBucket(key)->orgBucket->globalBucket. For streaming we could add connectionLimiter before tokenBucket. Pseudocode:
```
if endpoint == 'stream':
  if !acquire(connectionSlot): return 429_conn
  if !tokenBucket.consume(tokens): return 429_token
```
laura: UX: Console should display 'why 429' with top reason: per-key burst / org exhausted / connection limit / model fallback. That would cut down on support tickets.
maria: Ops-bot posted incident summary to #incidents with graph. Also need migration plan: immediate hotfix vs longer policy change.
ops-bot: auto-deploy finished. Canary at 10% with micro-burst smoothing for embeddings. Watch rolling metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/limits/canary
jon: Quick question — how do we handle rerank? It's synchronous but expensive CPU. Do we treat it like embed (unit count) or chat (token cost)?
ethan: Rerank should be per-request unit with weight multipliers, e.g., rerank=5 units per request. That aligns with billing and makes burst control straightforward.
laura: I'll sketch console mockups and an alert rule. Maria, can you coordinate a docs blurb explaining new 'ephemeral burst smoothing'?
maria: Yep. I'll draft and post in #docs and ping support. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
